entries.context: Krapf & Rebmann (1887) Nika-English Dictionary [v.n.] • Cross-verified with Lingua-Connect English–Giriama Dataset (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To take out little by little (from a bag), to snap off, to sprain
entries.context: Krapf & Rebmann (1887) Nika-English Dictionary [v.a.] • Cross-verified with Lingua-Connect English–Giriama Dataset (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To make known any disgrace or stigma attached to one (= Ku lombola)
entries.context: Krapf & Rebmann (1887) Nika-English Dictionary [v.a.] • Cross-verified with Lingua-Connect English–Giriama Dataset (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To cause to lean, to lean up or put up anything against another (v.c)

entries.english: To clamber, to climb with hands and feet, in contradistinction to Ku shombera
entries.context: Krapf & Rebmann (1887) Nika-English Dictionary [v.a.] • Cross-verified with Lingua-Connect English–Giriama Dataset (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To carry with both hands, to carry between two or more persons, to carry as ants and birds
entries.context: Krapf & Rebmann (1887) Nika-English Dictionary [v.a.] • Cross-verified with Lingua-Connect English–Giriama Dataset (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To step over from one stone to another in fording a river, to pass along a tree laid across a river

entries.english: To rub off, to set a newly forged instrument; to wipe off, to carry off, as water does earth and sand

entries.english: A drug which, when taken, is said to make one furious, and resolved to do anything, like the ndarama of the Waniasa

entries.translation: v., ku-ona, ku-sikira; to feel about, ku-hahasa, ku-gut'a-gut'a; I feel pain, naona utsungu; feel hurt, naona ku-lumira; I feel "all-overish," mwiri udzangira p'eho, hata sidzadima; feel queer, mwiri udzanihiririka; I feel cold, nasikira p'eho; hot, nasikira teri; I feel cool in danger, nidzasikira sogo-here (he ——, udzasikira k'aogo-here); I feel tired, nasikira kutsoka; feel for, as in the dark, or in dirty water, ku-wawata.
